facts.statement: Halcyornis is known from a single braincase fossil found in the Early Eocene London Clay of southeastern England.
facts.quote: It is known from a single neurocranium from the Early Eocene London Clay of southeastern England

facts.statement: The type specimen of Halcyornis holds the distinction of being the first fossil bird ever to receive a scientific name.
facts.quote: The type specimen of Halcyornis was the first fossil bird to be scientifically named.

facts.statement: In 1825, the type specimen was originally described as the gull species Larus toliapicus.
facts.quote: The type specimen of Halcyornis toliapicus was discovered and described in 1825 as Larus toliapicus and characterised as a small gull.

facts.statement: Richard Owen named the genus Halcyornis in 1846, referencing the kingfisher family.
facts.quote: In 1846, Richard Owen named the genus Halcyornis, in reference to the kingfishers

facts.statement: Only a single braincase is preserved, meaning the rest of the skeleton and the front of the skull are unknown.
facts.quote: The limited preservation of the single specimen of Halcyornis, part of a single braincase, precludes statements on the postcranial skeleton or for the rostral head.

facts.statement: The fossil shows that Halcyornis had olfactory lobes that were large compared to its forebrain.
facts.quote: The olfactory lobes were large relative to the telencephalon.

facts.statement: The wulst in Halcyornis was larger than in other Eocene birds related to parrots and songbirds and is similar in size to that of modern parrots.
facts.quote: The wulst is larger than in other Eocene psittacopasserans and is comparable in extent to that found in modern parrots.

facts.statement: Halcyornis belongs to the family Halcyornithidae, which includes Eocene birds found in Europe and North America.
facts.quote: Halcyornis is a member of the Halcyornithidae, a family of Eocene birds known from the early Eocene of Europe and North America.

facts.statement: The Halcyornithidae family is considered to be the basal relatives of both parrots and songbirds.
facts.quote: Halcyornithids are regarded as basal relatives of both parrots and songbirds.

facts.statement: In 2007, the genus was reassigned to the family Pseudasturidae based on skull similarities with Pseudasturides.
facts.quote: In 2007, the discovery of two new specimens of Pseudasturides with similar morphology of the skull to Halcyornis led to the reassignment of the genus to the family "Pseudasturidae".

facts.statement: Because Halcyornis is older than Pseudasturides, the family Pseudasturidae is now considered a junior synonym of Halcyornithidae.
facts.quote: As Halcyornis is an older taxon than Pseudasturides, "Pseudasturidae" is a junior synonym to Halcyornithidae, the proper name for the family of Eocene basal psittacopasserans.

facts.statement: Halcyornis lived during the Ypresian stage, between 56 and 48.07 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Ypresian to Ypresian (56 to 48.07 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Analysis of the ear structure predicts Halcyornis had a mean hearing value of 5900 Hz and was most sensitive to sounds around 3400 Hz.
rejected.quote: Halcyornis is predicted to have had a mean hearing value of 5900 Hz and to be most sensitive to sounds around 3400 Hz.
